page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.64-256 is a compute-focused flexible virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. The host is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor clocked at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 64 dedicated physical cores and 128 vCPUs with 2 threads per core, alongside 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring persistent or scratch data to be attached via external network block volumes. It features zero GPU hardware accelerators. For networking and external connectivity, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside its hypervisor network interfaces.

With 128 dedicated compute threads paired with moderate memory density, this profile emphasizes raw core count over high memory footprints. It is structured for compute-heavy parallel workloads, including continuous integration pipelines, batch processing clusters, scientific simulations, video encoding, and distributed container hosts.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.64-256 is a compute-aligned virtual machine configuration running on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J14 processor at 2.3 GHz. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores, operating 128 vCPUs with symmetric multi-threading, paired with 256.0 GB of system RAM. This configuration maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. The server does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote volume attachments for persistent storage needs. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By allocating a high volume of dedicated compute threads without the cost overhead of disproportionate memory allocations, VM.Standard.E5.Flex.64-256 offers high compute density. It is suited for parallel processing workloads, multi-threaded build systems, CPU-intensive microservices, and general compute tasks that do not demand expansive in-memory caching.
